# War Scroll Column 18 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 18 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 18:1 — "keeps covenant-faithfulness" vs. "keeps covenant faithfulness" vs. "keeps faith"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "keeps covenant-faithfulness" | Literal rendering of shomer chesed with hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "keeps covenant faithfulness" | Standard formal rendering without hyphen |
| PNEUMA | "keeps faith" | Simplified dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "keeps covenant faithfulness." The full phrase is needed to convey chesed in its covenantal context. PNEUMA's "keeps faith" is too generic — it loses the specifically covenantal dimension central to this hymn.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:2 — "ones stumbling" vs. "those who stumble" vs. "the weak"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the ones-stumbling" | Literal participle with hyphen |
| LOGOS | "those who stumble" | Standard formal English rendering of the participle |
| PNEUMA | "the weak" | Interpretive rendering — stumbling implies weakness |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "those who stumble." The Hebrew participle specifically means "stumbling" — not generic weakness. The image of the stumbling being called to mighty deeds is theologically significant and should not be flattened.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:2 — "wonderful mighty deeds" vs. "wondrous mighty deeds" vs. "wonders"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "wonderful-mighty-deeds" | Literal compound preserving both Hebrew terms |
| LOGOS | "wondrous mighty deeds" | Formal rendering keeping both adjective and noun |
| PNEUMA | "to do wonders" | Simplified dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "wondrous mighty deeds." Both Hebrew terms carry weight and should be preserved. PNEUMA's simplification to "wonders" loses the martial context (gevurot = mighty deeds/acts of power).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:3 — "destruction without remnant" vs. "destruction without remnant" vs. "wiped out completely"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "destruction-without-remnant" | Literal with hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "destruction without remnant" | Formal rendering preserving the Hebrew phrase |
| PNEUMA | "wiped out completely" | Dynamic paraphrase for impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "destruction without remnant." The phrase "without remnant" echoes the same language in col. 17:14 and must be rendered consistently. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses this verbal link.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:8 — "mysteries" vs. "mysteries" vs. "secrets"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "mysteries-of" | Literal construct of razei |
| LOGOS | "mysteries of" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "secrets of" | Accessible English equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "mysteries" (EMET/LOGOS). Per project convention, raz/razim is consistently rendered as "mystery/mysteries" throughout the DSS translations. PNEUMA's "secrets" does not carry the same theological weight.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Project convention.

---

## 18:13 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "steadfast love" vs. "unfailing love" for chesed

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "covenant-faithfulness" | Project standard rendering of chesed |
| LOGOS | "steadfast love" | Common English Bible rendering; hymnic register |
| PNEUMA | "unfailing love" | Accessible modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "covenant faithfulness" (without hyphen). Per project convention established in Gen 24, chesed is rendered "covenant-faithfulness." Consistency across the project overrides LOGOS's contextual variation, even in a hymnic passage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET. Project convention for chesed.

---
